rationale: The document claims 'you own all of the content' but immediately grants Facebook a 'non-exclusive, transferable, sub-licensable' license with vague termination rights ('letter or spirit' of terms, 'create risk or possible legal exposure'). Liability is capped at $100, users must indemnify Facebook for third-party claims, and termination can cut off all access. The false ownership framing combined with unilateral termination and liability waivers creates significant consumer risk.
evidence_quotes: You own all of the content and information you post on Facebook...you grant us a non-exclusive, transferable, sub-licensable, royalty-free, worldwide license
If you violate the letter or spirit of this Statement, or otherwise create risk or possible legal exposure for us, we can stop providing all or part of Facebook to you
OUR AGGREGATE LIABILITY...WILL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS ($100)
If anyone brings a claim against us related to your actions, content or information on Facebook, you will indemnify and hold us harmless
